# v0.5.0 - Parallel Codex subagent workflows

Codex Task Queue now turns repository workflow execution from a mostly serial process into a parallel multi-agent workflow.

## Highlights

- Generates executable workflow docs from product material, development notes, bug lists, and repository context.
- Supports project workflows through `docs/PRODUCT.md`, `docs/TASK_QUEUE.md`, and `docs/SESSION_RUNBOOK.md`.
- Supports maintenance workflows through `docs/PATCH_QUEUE.md` without requiring a product document.
- Runs independent `READY` tasks through multiple Codex subagents.
- Uses separate Git worktrees for parallel task execution.
- Preserves task handoffs, queue state, commits, and native Codex session history.

## Why it matters

Large AI coding tasks should not live as one long chat. This release makes Codex work more structured:

- workflow docs are generated before execution;
- humans can review and confirm the plan;
- independent work can run in parallel;
- every task keeps a handoff and commit boundary;
- blocked work remains visible instead of being hidden in chat history.

## Try it

```bash
node /path/to/codex-task-queue/scripts/codex-task-queue.mjs doctor
node /path/to/codex-task-queue/scripts/codex-task-queue.mjs init
node /path/to/codex-task-queue/scripts/codex-task-queue.mjs run --max-parallel 5
```

For maintenance queues:

```bash
node /path/to/codex-task-queue/scripts/codex-task-queue.mjs init --mode maintenance
node /path/to/codex-task-queue/scripts/codex-task-queue.mjs run --mode maintenance --max-parallel 5
```
